title: Show no clock, but log the time
statement: Don't show a clock unless speed is what the task measures, but quietly log how long learners take on each item and flag rushed answers.
example: One plan notes that the target test's publisher invalidates tests above 25% rapid guessing.
detail: A course plan keeps reading untimed because time pressure rewards rapid guessing, which the target test penalises; it keeps timing only where speed is the construct, such as fluency drills, and captures time on task silently everywhere for rapid-guess detection, with no clock on a reading passage (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5_build_2026_07_02/approval_clean.md`). An assessment plan notes that the test's publisher invalidates tests above 25% rapid guessing and that disengagement deflates scores, citing published work on low examinee effort, and has its proxy test capture per-item timing silently and flag rushing (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5_build_2026_07_02/mapproxy_clean.md`). A score with heavy rapid guessing is treated as invalid, since a disengaged attempt is not evidence of what a learner knows.
against: The 25% figure is the plan's account of the publisher's rule; nothing here checked it against the publisher's own documents. A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-deploy/BUILD-NOTES.md`).

The proxy captures per-item timing silently and flags rushing — so a disengaged student is coached before the official window, and a proxy score carries its own validity flag rather than silent noise.
